methodological_questions: Can a teammate drive before a PNR be identified reliably from the play-by-play and the derived play-type records?
Does a preceding teammate drive raise PNR PPP after controlling for player, lineup, opponent and game context?
How do label errors, outcome-derived labels and possession-ordering effects distort play-type PPP comparisons?
What sample size, sparsity and multiple-testing issues arise when comparing PNR possessions with and without a preceding drive?

historical_evidence.finding: Specific same-player and teammate X->Y sequences were ranked for PPP premiums above Y's baseline. Same-player L. Doncic DRIVE->PNR was +0.309 (n=53). D. Bane DRIVE->PNR was -0.324 (n=70, t=-2.7). Teammate Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR is shown as negative in FAM:SF-APPA-058. The record says most cells were DIRECT. It lists the mechanism as unclear, limited by label/classification error and small sample.

Play-type labeling audit. OTHER is inflated by 36% foul endings. DRIVE sits 12pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK). PNR shows a 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) map to a real play type via initiation_type. Verdict: artifact_found.

Season stability of top suppressors was tested; only 2/30 stars (7%) were stable. Negative teammate pairs include Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR -0.263 (n=31) and Tatum->Porzingis DRIVE->SPOT_UP -0.444 (n=31). Cells had a minimum n of 20. It is recorded as an adequately powered null with SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risk.

Label backfill verification FAILED overall. The PNR share was 28.7% against an expected 20-28% band. 3,100 games had a team PNR share above 33%. Team identity failed. 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated. 2024-25 PULL_UP was about 0-2% for many teams. League PNR PPP of 0.948 passed. It is recorded as label-error limited (921,514 possessions).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking player-level and teammate-pair X->Y sequence premiums, including DRIVE->PNR, to find consistent premiums
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as limited by label/classification error and small sample (n about 30-70 per cell). The mechanism is unclear and most cells were DIRECT.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing play-type PPP as if it were pure efficiency
failed_approaches.why: Foul endings inflate some types, DRIVE sits below the foul benchmark, PNR has a 22% foul rate, and initiation_type maps only 0.7% of possessions. Recorded as C_artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating teammate-specific sequential effects (including negative DRIVE->PNR pairs) as stable
failed_approaches.why: Adequately powered null (B_powered_null). Only 2/30 stars were stable, with small cells and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risk.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Relying on backfilled play-type labels (including PNR) as accurate
failed_approaches.why: Backfill verification failed on PNR share, team identity and PULL_UP; 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy-calibrated (C_artifact, LABEL_ERROR).

evidence_establishes: Recorded DRIVE->PNR premiums are heterogeneous in sign: Doncic +0.309 in FAM:SF40, Bane -0.324 and Giannis->Lillard -0.263 in FAM:SF-APPA-058. This does not support a universal 'any' claim.
The derived play-type labels are flawed: PNR labels are mostly proxy-calibrated, the PNR share is out of band, and play-type PPP is contaminated by foul endings (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPA-030).
Pair-level sequential premiums have been unstable or underpowered (FAM:SF-APPA-058, FAM:SF40).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the pooled average effect of a teammate drive on PNR PPP is positive, zero or negative.
Whether the heterogeneity reflects real player effects or label noise and small samples; FAM:SF40 records the mechanism as unclear.
Whether labeling quality has improved since those audits, or whether a drive-before-PNR flag can be built directly from raw play-by-play without the proxy labels.
Anything causal: the records concern PPP premiums above baseline, not adjusted or causal estimates.
own_inferences: The word 'any' makes the hypothesis a universal claim, which one negative well-powered subgroup would falsify. The only sensible test is of the pooled average effect plus its heterogeneity.

A DRIVE->PNR sequence conditions on the possession continuing after the drive. Drives ending in a shot, foul or turnover are excluded by construction, so PNR PPP after a drive is selected on survival and could be biased up or down.
DRIVE labeling is partly outcome-derived (foul leakage), and PNR PPP includes foul endings. A naive comparison could therefore reflect labeling rather than efficiency.
Drive-before-PNR may mark particular lineups, players (such as rim-pressure guards) and game states, so confounding is likely. Matching or fixed effects are needed.
A feasible version is a pooled, label-robust estimate with shrinkage across players. Pair-specific claims are not feasible given the n of about 30-70 recorded in FAM:SF40 and FAM:SF-APPA-058.
uncertainties: The size and direction of the pooled effect are unknown.
The current accuracy of the PNR and DRIVE labels in the graph database is unknown, as is whether raw play-by-play can support an independent sequence definition.

The tool results are truncated, and the full texts of FAM:SF40 and FAM:SF-APPA-058 were not read. FAM:SF-APPA-030 names related families that were not returned or read, so no claim is made about them.
The 2025-26 playoffs are incomplete on the question date, and the 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13.
The possession-ordering and time-window definition of 'preceding' is unspecified in the question.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the records, a naive pooled comparison might look feasible. The records show sign-heterogeneous DRIVE->PNR cells, label artifacts (foul leakage, proxy-calibrated PNR labels) and a failed label verification. They also show that pair-level sequential effects are underpowered or unstable. I therefore moved to proceed_with_changes: reframe the claim as an average effect with heterogeneity, validate labels first, and control for the survival selection.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR labels are 82.8% proxy-calibrated and the backfill failed verification (FAM:SF-APPA-030). Without independently validated drive and PNR flags, the exposure and outcome are both mismeasured.
Foul endings inflate or deflate play-type PPP (FAM:SF-CHT-025). PPP must be computed on a label-independent outcome definition.
Player-pair and player-level DRIVE->PNR cells have n of about 30-70 with unstable results (FAM:SF40, FAM:SF-APPA-058). Only pooled or hierarchical estimates are feasible.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work estimated DRIVE->PNR premiums for individual players and pairs, with mixed signs, small n and label-error limits. It did not give a pooled, adjusted estimate. Label audits found foul-ending artifacts and failed backfill verification. The universal claim is not supported at the cell level, and the pooled question remains open.

risks.text: Proxy-calibrated PNR labels and failed backfill verification could misclassify both the drive and the PNR.
Foul endings and the DRIVE label's dependence on outcomes can produce spurious PPP differences.

Defining the exposure by the sequence of events conditions on the possession surviving the drive. Only information available before the PNR begins may be used to define the exposure and comparison set.
Players, lineups, opponent defense, score and clock state, and era may drive both the drive-before-PNR rate and PNR efficiency.
Heterogeneity analysis by player or pair is underpowered (n about 30-70 per cell).
Testing many player or pair cells will yield false positives (the SF40 ranking was top-of-list).
Choosing the top and bottom cells (Doncic, Bane, George) invites regression to the mean.
Label quality varies by season (2024-25 PULL_UP near zero) and play style changes, so effects may differ across seasons.
Teammate drives immediately before a labeled PNR are a small fraction of PNR possessions.

design.estimand: Average difference in PNR PPP between possessions with and without a teammate (non-ball-handler) DRIVE in the preceding window, adjusted for player and context. Also report the share of players or pairs with a positive effect and the between-player heterogeneity (tau), so that the 'any' claim is evaluated explicitly.
design.unit: PNR possession (initiator-level), nested in game, team and ball handler.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 through 2024-25 (regular season and playoffs) and the 2025-26 regular season. The 2025-26 playoffs are excluded because they are incomplete on 2026-06-14, or held out as a later confirmation set. Exposure is a teammate drive flag built from raw play-by-play (shot distance, action type, clock) within a pre-specified window of N seconds before the PNR, not only from the derived labels. Primary sample is PNR possessions where the PNR is not the first action, plus a matched comparison.
design.power: Compute counts first. Pre-specify the minimum detectable PPP difference at 80% power with a variance of about 1.2 per possession. Proceed only if the pooled sample detects 0.05 PPP or less. Player and pair level estimates use hierarchical shrinkage and are descriptive, with no cell-level confirmatory claims at n of about 30-70.
design.controls: Ball-handler and screener fixed effects, lineup or on-court quality, opponent defense, score margin, period and clock, home/away, season, and possession start type. Match or stratify on elapsed possession time to address the survival selection. Compute PPP using a foul-robust definition (a sensitivity analysis with and without foul-ending possessions, and with free throws attributed by possession). Validate drive and PNR labels on a hand-audited sample of at least 300 sequences, and require at least 90% agreement before the main analysis.
design.falsification: Placebo exposure: a teammate drive after the PNR, or at a random time in the possession, should show no effect. A non-drive teammate action (such as a pass) as the preceding event serves as a negative control. A label-shuffle test and a split-sample season replication guard against label artifacts. Re-estimate the effect after dropping the foul-ending possessions flagged in FAM:SF-CHT-025.
design.multiplicity: One primary pooled estimate (alpha 0.05). Secondary analyses (by season, by ball handler, by drive distance) are exploratory, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 0.10. Do not select cells by extreme values (RTM).
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the pooled adjusted effect is positive with a 95% CI excluding 0 and at least +0.03 PPP, it replicates in the held-out season, it survives the foul-robust sensitivity analysis, and the placebo effects are null. Reject the universal 'any' claim if heterogeneity shows a credible subgroup with a negative effect. Call it a powered null if the CI lies within +/-0.03. If label validation fails (below 90%), return untestable or artifact.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the derived graph-database possession records as of 2026-06-14, with a frozen snapshot hash recorded. The 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13. The 2025-26 playoffs are excluded or treated as partial and held out.

methodological_questions: Can a drive preceding a PNR be identified reliably from play-by-play and derived play-type records?
Does a preceding teammate drive causally raise PNR PPP after controlling for player, lineup, opponent and game context?
How do label errors, outcome-derived labels and possession-ordering/lookahead affect play-type PPP comparisons?
What sample size, exposure sparsity and multiple-testing issues arise when comparing PNR possessions with versus without a preceding drive?

You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

reasoning_details.text:
I could call a few more tools to read the remaining families for detail, but the budget is fine and finishing now is more efficient, so I'll wrap up and write careful citations. The core question asks whether any teammate's DRIVE before a PNR raises that PNR's PPP, but a universal "any" claim can't really be tested as stated, and the SF40 numbers show the effect varies a lot, with Doncic's same-player DRIVE-to-PNR at +0.309 among the cases to weigh.

I'm checking the remaining evidence: the SF40 outcome shows Bane's DRIVE-to-PNR at -0.324 and Giannis-to-Lillard at -0.263, so teammate effects point in both directions. The labels also look weak, since most PNR tags are proxy-calibrated, many PNR shares fail, and DRIVE tags may leak foul outcomes. Several statuses ("not a hypothesis test," "artifact," "rejected," "inconclusive") mean I should present this as uncertain rather than settled. I'll frame the answer as a pooled average with heterogeneity and a matched design, restricting to drives within the same possession.

I'm now weighing how to assign probabilities to the possible verdicts: a literal "any" claim looks hard to support, a rejection due to heterogeneity seems plausible, and artifacts and untestability also carry real weight. I'm also excluding the 2025-26 playoffs from the frozen dataset since they weren't complete by the cutoff date.

reasoning_details.text:
I could call a few more tools to read the remaining families for detail, but the budget is fine and finishing now is more efficient, so I'll wrap up and write careful citations. The core question asks whether any teammate's DRIVE before a PNR raises that PNR's PPP, but a universal "any" claim can't really be tested as stated, and the SF40 numbers show the effect varies a lot, with Doncic's same-player DRIVE-to-PNR at +0.309 among the cases to weigh.

I'm checking the remaining evidence: the SF40 outcome shows Bane's DRIVE-to-PNR at -0.324 and Giannis-to-Lillard at -0.263, so teammate effects point in both directions. The labels also look weak, since most PNR tags are proxy-calibrated, many PNR shares fail, and DRIVE tags may leak foul outcomes. Several statuses ("not a hypothesis test," "artifact," "rejected," "inconclusive") mean I should present this as uncertain rather than settled. I'll frame the answer as a pooled average with heterogeneity and a matched design, restricting to drives within the same possession.

I'm now weighing how to assign probabilities to the possible verdicts: a literal "any" claim looks hard to support, a rejection due to heterogeneity seems plausible, and artifacts and untestability also carry real weight. I'm also excluding the 2025-26 playoffs from the frozen dataset since they weren't complete by the cutoff date.
